result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in 103 seconds on one thread with a peak of 1.45 to 1.53 GB, and reproduces every target except two Wilcoxon p-values. Two runs of the finished script (md5 c11e3c99f8dcd8a3a4f45447a324f9b5, 725 lines) gave byte-identical CSV files.

The two departures are a matter of method. The issue text quotes p = 0.007 (all libraries) and 0.012 (without zr3534_4), which are normal approximations; the exact test gives 0.005 and 0.010. The same paragraph quotes the exact value for the heat cohort (0.008), so it mixed the two methods. The script writes both for every comparison.

Three findings go beyond the targets and change how I-09 should read:
- **Cohort is associated with the excess.** The Fisher test on the 13 carriers gives p = 0.19, as in the issue. Under a stricter rule (all 54 CpGs at the cutoff: 1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012. As a continuous quantity the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). Ploidy shows nothing (p = 0.39, 1, 0.56, 0.70).
- **The excess is in every library.** All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.31 to 32 times); the 9 "without the excess" are at 1.31 to 4.83.
- **The block is not simply single-copy.** Counting all 3,570 30-mers, 2,471 (69.2%) occur once and 874 exactly twice. Of the second copies, 868 lie in three places on other linkage groups, none of which reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times in the reference.

The script also checks its inputs against each other and stops on any mismatch. It recomputes each library's median, cutoff and number of CpGs at the cutoff from the raw file, rebuilds the normalized counts of the united table from the raw counts (which fixes the library order), and confirms that its pooled differences equal step 05's meth.diff to 1e-8. Independent cross-checks agree: awk on two raw files, a Python reading of the reference, pwilcox and dhyper by hand, and all 176 per-library and 54 per-CpG values of the verifying agent's tables.

Nothing outside `06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563*` was edited. An early snapshot of the script was committed by the parent session (40cd66d, "unreviewed"); the working-tree file is the finished one.

design_decisions: The DML region is read from step 07 (dml_regions_legacy.csv, largest run of ploidy DML), so its coordinates are not typed in. This adds a dependency on step 07 beyond the step 05 tables. The script stops if that run is not on NC_047563.1.
The window is the DML region plus 10 kb on either side (39623323 to 39645520), close to the suggested 39,625,000 to 39,645,000. The script stops if the block and its 5 kb flanks do not fit.

Block rule: a CpG has excess coverage when at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff; such CpGs within 1 kb form a run; the block is the run that holds the DML region. I chose the cutoff because it is the criterion by which corrected mode removes a CpG, not to match the target.

Carrier rule: at least one tested CpG of the region at or above the library's cutoff. Because the Fisher result for cohort depends on the rule, the script also reports a stricter rule (every CpG at the cutoff) and Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess, on two scales.

Per-library medians over a zone use only the CpG sites with reads in that library, as the library median does. In the per-CpG profile a library without reads counts as 0. Both are stated in the header.
Coverage relative to the cutoff is written per library as a ratio and per CpG as the number of libraries at or above the cutoff, not as a per-CpG ratio.

Leave-one-out applies the difference rule only, as instructed, and the output says each count is therefore the largest possible number of DML. I added one row for the 9 libraries without the excess taken alone.
Wilcoxon tests are exact, with the normal approximation written beside each for part d. The script stops if two libraries tie on percent methylation.

Part f counts all 3,570 30-mers of the block, not only the sample of 60, which is kept for comparison. It also reports where the second copies of the two-copy 30-mers lie and whether any library reaches its cutoff there. The latter costs no second pass: the first pass keeps every position at or above the cutoff.

The summary has four columns (section, quantity, value, how_defined), one more than specified. Values are text: a number, a label, 'x of y' or 'a to b'. Setting values are interpolated into the definitions.
The script calls setDTthreads(1), so the stated run time and memory hold on a shared machine.
The profile carries extra columns: zone, DML flags, step 05's meth.diff for tested CpGs, libraries with reads, and min and max relative coverage per class.
left_out: No model refit in the leave-one-out (the verifying agent used glm with p < 2e-4): left out by instruction.
Share of soft-masked bases in the block (the agent's 10%): not computed, because Biostrings drops letter case and it was not a target.
Relative coverage at the three places that hold second copies: the script reports only whether the cutoff is reached there (it is not), because medians would need a second pass over the 22 files.
Coverage beyond 10 kb either side of the region (the agent looked at 100 kb): not in the script.
README.md and issues.md were not edited, by rule; proposed text is in the caveats and in readme_row.
caveats: The cohort difference in the size of the excess cannot be attributed. Cohort, stock and sequencing batch coincide (I-01, I-08), and control libraries are somewhat higher within both classes, so part of it may be a batch effect on the coverage of this GC-richer block.

'Carries the excess' is a threshold on a continuous quantity. Three heat triploids sit just above it (zr3534_6, _7, _8: 1.04 to 1.22 times the cutoff, 29 to 42 of 54 CpGs), and they are what moves the Fisher p for cohort from 0.19 to 0.012.

The issue's sentence that the heat loci are 'not methylation regulated by heat' is supported for the 22-library analysis: without zr3534_4 the median heat difference is -5.66 points and no CpG passes. Among the 9 libraries without the excess, 24 CpGs still exceed 20 points for heat and 37 for ploidy, with groups of 3 and 6. That reflects the four heat-cohort diploids at 34% to 43% and is description only.
Each library is treated as one animal. The sample sheet names the animal for the heat cohort only (I-36).
Run time was measured with the machine under load (load average about 5). Peak memory varied between 1.45 and 1.53 GB across runs.
The 06_diagnostics README needs the row below and the line `Rscript 06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R` in its run list.
An exploration file (explore_window.rds) was written to the repository root by mistake early on and moved to scratch within a minute.

Exploration not in the script, so not reproducible from the repository: within 100 kb either side no CpG outside the block reaches a cutoff, and median coverage at the two larger second-copy places is ordinary in all 22 libraries.

Proposed text for issues.md, I-09, bullet 1: The block of excess coverage is NC_047563.1:39,633,065-39,636,662 (3.6 kb, 82 CpG sites, 56 of them tested, all removed by the filter): the CpGs at which at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff. The 5 kb on either side have ordinary coverage (0.56 to 1.72 times the library median) and no CpG at the cutoff. The ends are those of the cutoff rule; the nearest CpG sites, 182 and 183 bp away, are at 2.5 and 1.3 times the library median in the libraries with the excess.

Proposed text, bullet 2 (replaces 'The excess is not in every animal ... no association with ploidy or cohort'): The excess is in every library and differs in size. All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.3 to 32 times). In 13 the median coverage of the 54 tested CpGs is 10.6 to 35.5 times the library median and reaches the cutoff; in the other 9 it is 2.0 to 5.9 times, with no CpG at the cutoff. The 13 are found in all four groups (4 of 10 heat, 9 of 12 control; 5 of 11 diploid, 8 of 11 triploid). Ploidy shows no difference (Fisher exact p = 0.39; size of the excess, Wilcoxon p = 0.56). Cohort does: the Fisher test on the 13 gives p = 0.19, but with all 54 CpGs required at the cutoff (1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012, and the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). A repeat carried equally by every animal would not give this spread. The pattern is a copy-number difference among individual animals that is larger in the control cohort; cohort, stock and sequencing batch cannot be separated (I-01, I-08).

Proposed text, bullet 3: keep, with 'at most 1 ploidy DML' and add: all 54 CpGs have q < 0.01, so the 20-point rule alone decides; the counts are recomputed differences without a refit; leaving out any other single library leaves 50 to 53 and 29 to 53; zr3534_4 supplies 39% of the heat group's normalized reads. The 9 libraries without the excess alone (6 diploid, 3 triploid; 6 heat, 3 control) still give 37 and 24 CpGs above 20 points.

Proposed text, bullet 4: replace 'Wilcoxon p = 0.007, and p = 0.012 without zr3534_4' by 'exact Wilcoxon p = 0.005, and p = 0.010 without zr3534_4'. The heat cohort (0.008) and control cohort (0.09) values stand.

Proposed text, bullet 5 (replaces 'mostly single-copy'): 69% of the block's 30-mers occur once in the reference (2,471 of 3,570; 42 of 60 in the first sample). 874 occur exactly twice; 474, 294 and 100 of the second copies lie at NC_047560.1:13,874,789-13,881,520, NC_047559.1:4,498,648-4,509,003 and NC_047561.1:36,696,412-36,696,653, where no CpG reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times. The block is not in the transposable element track (nearest records 799 bp before and 585 bp after). It lies inside introns of LOC105317102 and LOC105318567, and 3,471 of its 3,599 bases lie in the lncRNA gene LOC105341636, exons and introns at the same coverage (18.9 and 20.5 times the library median), so the extra copies are genomic. GC content is 42.5% against 30.9% and 32.7% in the flanks.

The script is written, runs from the repository root in about 4 minutes (3.7 to 4.1 measured, single thread, peak 1.2 to 1.5 GB), and two consecutive runs of the finished script gave byte-identical CSV files (md5 compared). It reads only step 05 and step 07 tables, the seven tracks and the sample sheet; the raw coverage files are not needed.

What it computes, for both modes, both DML lists and seven tracks (264 rows in feature_odds_matched.csv): (1) odds ratios against all tested and against eligible CpGs, checked in the script against step 07 (all 56 cells equal; the script stops otherwise); (2) Mantel-Haenszel within 5-point methylation bins; (3) within bin and decile of within-group SD; (4) ranges 5-95 and 15-85; (5) transposable elements by coverage quartile; (6) CDS against intron within genes; (7) block-bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples of 100 kb windows) for 1 (eligible), 2 and 3; (8) for ploidy, 1,000 label permutations within cohort, plus 1,000 that also keep the acute heat shock balanced.

Legacy results, ploidy then heat. Gene body: 7.08 and 6.14 against all tested; 2.52 and 2.20 against eligible; 2.04 and 1.68 within methylation bins; 1.13 (block interval 0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36) within bin and SD decile. After matching: CDS 1.25 and 1.17, intron 0.81 and 0.87, transposable element 1.05 and 1.02, intergenic 0.80 and 0.92. Shuffled ploidy labels (within cohort): gene-body odds ratio against eligible CpGs median 2.61 (2.5th to 97.5th percentile 1.41 to 4.47), the real 2.52 reached in 54.7% of permutations; median 742.5 CpGs called per permutation (5th to 95th percentile 532 to 1,376), 13.5% reach 1,038. Corrected mode reads the same (gene body 2.85 to 1.24 for ploidy, 2.02 to 0.94 for heat after matching; permutation median 3.11, real value reached in 66.5%).

One addition beyond the task list, because issues.md changed while I worked (commit 68a8a1b, 07:14, added a fifth row to the second table of I-41 from a scratch run): the script also computes the matched comparison 3 for every shuffled-label list, with the within-group SD and its deciles recomputed for the groups the shuffled labels define. Result (legacy, within cohort): gene body median 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), real 1.13 reached in 44%; CDS median 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. With acute heat shock also balanced: 1.08 (0.58 to 2.33) and 1.17 (0.83 to 1.44), 26%. This reproduces the integration check's 1.10 (0.58 to 2.33), 1.18 (0.87 to 1.46) and 29%. The script therefore now writes all five rows of that table.

q-value rule, counted from the diffmeth tables: for ploidy every CpG above 20 points also has q below 0.01 (1,038 of 1,038 legacy, largest q 0.0046; 952 of 952 corrected, largest q 0.0052), and the script stops if that fails. For heat one CpG of 2,352 fails the q rule in legacy mode (q 0.018), none of 2,273 in corrected mode. Heat rows in both permutation tables carry NA and the sentence that no permutation exists.

Two targets depart, both explained under targets: transposable element in the top coverage quartile for ploidy is 0.21, not 0.20 (the script keeps the one ploidy DML outside the eligible range, as step 07 does); the share of eligible CpGs called at a mean of 10% to 20% is 0.37%, not 0.30% (the 300-permutation run under-sampled labellings with very many calls; issues.md already says 0.3% to 0.4%).

Checks done outside the script (scratch, not reproducible from the repository): the Mantel-Haenszel estimates were recomputed with table() and mantelhaen.test on factors (identical); the block intervals with a slow weighted-table implementation (identical at 200 resamples); 40 permutations per scheme and mode were recomputed without pruning and with table() plus fisher.test (counts and all seven odds ratios identical); 25 permutations per scheme for the matched odds ratios (identical in legacy, within 4e-4 in corrected, one CpG at a decile boundary); the pruning of never-callable CpGs was identical to full evaluation on 40 permutations.

Same lists, same matching: gene body 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), CDS 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. Matched row: 1.13 (0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36). design_decisions: Convention of step 07 kept in every comparison: all DML of a list against the CpGs of the background that are not in the list. DML outside the background stay in the DML row; the notes column counts them (1 for 10-90, 39 and 73 for 15-85 in legacy mode).

Estimators: unstratified odds ratios are the conditional estimates of fisher.test (identical to step 07); stratified ones are the common odds ratio and interval of stats::mantelhaen.test. A vectorised Mantel-Haenszel formula used for the resamples is checked against mantelhaen.test inside the script. No literature is cited, because I could not check the papers.

Strata: 5-point bins closed on the left over 0 to 100; deciles of within-group SD among eligible CpGs (global, not within bin). Strata without a DML, without another CpG, or without variation in the track add nothing; the output gives strata used and DML in them.
Within-group SD: pooled around the four group means (ploidy by cohort), 18 degrees of freedom, one matrix formula used for the real and the shuffled labels.

Block interval: percentile bootstrap, 2,000 resamples of the 100 kb windows that hold a compared CpG (4,399 legacy, 4,348 corrected), the same resamples for every list, track and comparison of a mode; the Fisher conditional estimate is recomputed on each resample. Bootstrap rather than jackknife because the jackknife interval assumes a normal log odds ratio, which fails where one window holds most DML of a track (53 of 65 ploidy DML in lncRNA).

Permutation as specified (within cohort, 5 and 5, 6 and 6), 1,000 draws, the same labellings for both modes. A second scheme (also balanced on acute heat shock, 3 and 3, 2 and 2) is reported beside it, because the verification used it and the real labels are balanced over it. Results barely differ except in the upper tail of the counts.

The 20-point rule is evaluated on cross-multiplied whole numbers, so a difference of exactly 20 is never called through rounding (in scratch, floating-point arithmetic called 9 of 25 such ties in 40 permutations). With the real labels this rule reproduces the step 05 list exactly; the script checks it.

CpGs whose per-library percentages span no more than the threshold are skipped in the permutation loop. This is exact (a pooled percentage is a weighted mean) and was confirmed against full evaluation in scratch; it brings 1,000 permutations from about 75 to about 15 seconds.

result.verdict:
The script is sound and can be accepted after small changes. No reported number is wrong and no check is vacuous.

- **Runs:** three runs in the repository and one in a clean copy of HEAD (made with `git archive`) all exit 0 without a warning. They take 88 to 108 seconds on one thread with a peak of 1.53 GB. The four CSV files are byte-identical across all runs and with the committed copies.
- **Numbers:** every value of the four tables was reproduced with code that shares nothing with the script (mawk on the raw files, base R without data.table or the helpers, hand-written quantile, Fisher and exact Wilcoxon, mawk on the GFF and BED tracks, Python with numpy on the reference).
- **Checks:** I evaluated the script's own check lines on altered objects. Exchanged library columns, one count off by one, exchanged ploidy labels, another difference threshold and positions shifted by one base each stop the script.
- **Code rules:** library order, strata, coordinates (0-based starts, BED, GFF, 1-based sequence), data.table scoping, paths and the style rules hold. No random numbers are used.

One finding is medium. The header and two summary definitions call the leave-one-out counts the largest possible number of DML. That is false for four libraries (zr3534_1, zr3534_5, zr3534_10, zr3644_17), because 1 to 4 further CpGs of the region become testable without them. The result for zr3534_4 is not affected. The four low findings concern how values are written (a padded "   1", a p-value whose three digits have already been re-rounded to 0.012 in the handoff, a tie created by rounding in the per-library table, two coordinate conventions in one notation).

For issues.md, one sentence of I-09 is not what the script gives: block over flanks is 1.3 to 4.8 and 10.8 to 32.0, not 1.3 to 5.3 and 10.8 to 33.9, which come from another definition. "Mostly single-copy" should carry the full count (69% of the 30-mers once, 874 twice in three places on other linkage groups). "1 ploidy DML" is "at most 1" from the script. The soft-masked shares are not computed by any script.

`R.utils`, needed to read the .gz tables, is not in the `load_packages()` call; this is the known pipeline-wide finding and here it would fail only after the 22 coverage files are read.

I changed nothing in the repository. design_decisions: Extract: first 6 Mb of NC_047559.1, 300 kb around NC_047563.1:39,633,323, the mitochondrial sequence, five unplaced scaffolds (one with coverage 6 to 11 times the median, two with many tested CpGs, one on which a file begins, one that 12 libraries lack), and the position of the first line of every file taken from every library. Lines stay in file order and percentages are carried as text, so the files are lines of the originals; written to tempdir() and deleted at the end.

methylKit's route follows the task: legacy mode leaves methRead at header = TRUE with mincov = config$import_min_coverage and filters with lo.count only; corrected mode passes header = FALSE and hi.perc. It is run twice per mode, once per treatment vector, as the legacy script did; the helper route uses reorganize() as step 05 does.

The helper route calls read_filtered_counts, key_to_position, scale_counts_like_methylkit, make_methylraw, unite and reorganize in the order of fit_mode() in step 05. Step 05 does not offer that chain as a function, so the chain is repeated, not reimplemented.

Both routes are tested with the covariates as step 05 passes them, so they differ only in how the counts are built. The legacy coding (character vectors, built from the sample sheet and checked against the vectors typed in the legacy script) is fitted once more on methylKit's route in both modes: legacy mode is then the legacy call end to end, and corrected mode is that call with its two defects fixed.

Three rules, in a column of the table. identical: counts, positions and sets; any difference fails. tolerance: floating-point values; fails above a relative difference of 1e-12, and n_different still counts values that are not bit-identical. recorded: an expected difference, not judged (step 04's order, p and q under the legacy coding, the corrected CpG set of step 05 against the extract). The script stops at the end if any judged row differs, after writing the tables.

Under the legacy coding meth.diff and the DML lists are judged and p-values and q-values are recorded. The DML lists of legacy mode must be those of the legacy call, so a difference there should stop the script.

A whole-library part beyond the task: import and filter of six libraries through methylKit and through the helper, and against the records of step 05. This is the statement of I-05 and of the helper comment, and it covers the real cutoffs (59 to 112 reads), which the extract cannot.
A part beyond the task that ties the tables step 05 wrote to the raw counts inside the regions, so the equivalence is tied to the files the pipeline uses.

Synthetic counts: 20 sets of four libraries of 30,001 CpGs after set.seed(20261119), three draws per CpG and two per set; medians chosen so that the factors are 1, 1.5, 1.25 and one arbitrary ratio, which forces exact ties.

Step 04's order is checked on rows selected by step 04's own rule, at 1 read and at config$min_coverage reads, with the effect on percent methylation and on the correlations; at config$min_coverage the selection must reproduce the united CpGs and factors of the helper route or the script stops.
Three small CSV files (25 KB, 10 KB, 2 KB); nothing per CpG. The main table carries the methylKit version.
left_out: methylKit's own route on the 22 whole libraries at once: not run, because it needs about 9 GB against a limit of 3 GB. In its place: both routes on the extract, import and filter on six whole libraries, the counts of step 05 against raw counts, and the synthetic ties.
Whole-library comparison for the other 16 libraries: left out for run time (about 13 s per library and mode; all 22 in both modes would add about 7 minutes).

The tie of the tables of step 05 to the raw counts outside the regions of the extract (a second agent's 31.7 and 30.0 million values): not done; only the lines of the regions are kept. It could be added to the extraction pass for about half a minute if wanted.
Nothing of task items (a) to (e) or of the step 04 check is left out. Legacy mode has no upper cutoff to compare, because no upper filter runs there.
caveats: On the extract the corrected-mode cutoffs are 182 to 701 reads, against 59 to 112 on the whole files, because the extract is rich in deeply covered sequence. The same rule runs at other values: the upper filter removes 2,628 rows there, and 200 of the 363 mitochondrial CpGs stay in the united table. Cutoffs of the whole files are exercised only in the six whole libraries.

No first-line CpG has 10 reads in all 22 libraries, so the first-line rule changes rows per library (8 libraries at import, 1 among the kept rows) and never the united table. That is a property of the data.

The sentence in 06_diagnostics/README.md that no comparison on the complete 22 libraries in corrected mode is on record stays true in the strict sense: for whole libraries the script compares import and filter of six. Which CpGs each mode keeps on the whole files is checked by the sibling script coverage_filter_variants.R.
The helper chain is copied from fit_mode(). If step 05 changes its chain this script must follow; a stale table of step 05 would be caught only inside the regions.

The header sentence on the glm.fit warnings rests on a scratch test, not on the script: 1,433 of the 1,435 CpGs with a warning in legacy mode have methylated reads only in libraries of one ploidy and one cohort. The header says it was looked at once.
The header statements on what methylKit does were checked against the installed 1.28.0 source only.

The script is long (933 lines) and does more than the task lists: whole libraries, the two legacy defects, the legacy coding, the tie to the tables of step 05. A reviewer should read those parts as additions.
Run time depends on the machine: the earlier version took 7.3 minutes when quiet and 10.8 minutes under load; the final version took 9.0 minutes twice with two other R processes running.
My scratch directory still holds two copies of the extract (232 MB) and the awk recount; nothing there is needed by the script.

findings.summary: The tail statistics of the label permutation (95th percentile of CpGs called, share of permutations reaching the real number, share of eligible CpGs called by methylation bin, 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) carry a large Monte Carlo error at 1,000 draws, and nothing in the output says so. The two schemes differ on these cells by sampling error only, yet the tables read as a scheme effect.

My complete enumeration of all 232,848 labellings (110,880 balanced on the heat shock): 95th percentile 1,386.8 and 1,461.0; share 0.1283 (29,878 labellings) and 0.1379 (15,288); 10-20% bin 0.386% and 0.403%; median 752 and 749; 5th percentile 520 and 521; gene-body odds ratio median 2.65 (1.46 to 4.52) and 2.65 (1.47 to 4.46), real value reached in 56.2% and 56.4%. Corrected mode: script 1,304 and 1,683, 0.147 and 0.175; exact 1,327 and 1,395, 0.149 and 0.158. The 95th percentile of 1,000 random labellings has a central 95% range of 1,238 to 1,675 (within cohort) and 1,281 to 1,853 (balanced); a value of 1,748 or more occurs in 4.6% of such samples. The enumeration reproduces numbers that I-06 reports from another computation (903 of 924, median 1,530; 40 of 252, median 753.5). Scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/review2-feature_odds_matched/work/check_G_enumeration.R, out/G_legacy.log, out/G_corrected.log, out/E_legacy.log.
findings.suggested_fix: For the count summaries (median, percentiles, share reaching the real number, share called by bin and by track) replace the draws by the complete enumeration: pooled counts of the 126 heat-cohort subsets (one of each mirror pair) and the 924 control-cohort subsets on the candidate CpGs, added pairwise; the balanced scheme is a subset. In plain R this took 8 to 9 minutes and 2.3 GB per mode. If that is too long, keep the draws and write beside every percentile its order-statistic 95% interval (here 1,266 to 1,666 and 1,448 to 2,113 for the two 95th percentiles) and beside every share its standard error, and say in the notes column that the schemes differ by sampling error only. The 1,000 draws can stay for the matched odds ratios, with the same intervals.

findings.evidence: 61,056 eligible CpGs give quantile indices 1 + (n - 1)p = 12212, 24423, 36634, 48845 for p = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8. seq(0, 1, length.out = 11)[7] is 0.6000000000000001, so the third index is 36634.000000000007 and that cut is interpolated a hair above the CpG; the other three equal the CpG exactly. findings.summary: The identity check between methylKit's floating-point rule and the script's exact rule stops the run if a CpG lies at exactly the threshold and its stored difference rounds above it. Such ties exist in the real data.

result.verdict:
Accept the script. It computes what the task asked, and every number I recomputed with independent code agrees with it; the one change needed before its permutation counts are quoted is a Monte Carlo interval or a complete enumeration.

- **Runs:** two runs from the repository root finished with exit 0 in 238 s each, 1.30 GB peak, one thread, empty stderr. The four CSV files were byte-identical between the runs and to the copies taken beforehand; the script and repository were left unchanged.
- **Reading:** I found no error in strata, group assignment, library order, coordinates, seeds, data.table scoping or paths. The header is accurate, there is no em dash and no "desiccation", and every file read is tracked in git.
- **Recomputation:** base R with my own track reader, overlap rule, conditional odds ratio, Mantel-Haenszel estimate and SD by residuals reproduced all 180 non-bootstrap odds rows, 50 of the 52 block intervals I recomputed (the other two differ by 0.0001), and 361 of 364 permutation cells. All permutation counts are identical. The differences trace to fisher.test's root tolerance and to one CpG on a decile cut.
- **Checks can fail:** three mutated scratch copies (shifted eligible range, CpG shifted by one base, two libraries exchanged) all stopped at the intended check.
- **The medium finding:** the 95th percentile of the count, the share reaching the real number and the share called by bin are unstable at 1,000 draws. The scheme with acute heat shock balanced drew a heavy tail (95th percentile 1,748 against an exact 1,461). The within-cohort scheme the task specified is close to exact (1,376 against 1,387; 13.5% against 12.8%).
- **Low findings:** six, none of which changes a reading.
- **issues.md:** fifteen sentences of I-41 and I-06 need the script's values. No conclusion of I-41 changes: the gene-body excess is gone after matching (1.13 and 1.01) and is reached by shuffled labels in more than half of the labellings. Confirmed without change: the first table, both range sentences, CDS against intron, transposable elements by coverage in both modes, the SD medians and the corrected-mode sentence.
- **Corrected mode adds:** matched gene body 1.24 (block interval 0.85 to 1.96) and 0.94 (0.73 to 1.27). The matched intergenic odds ratio for ploidy stays below 1 (0.59, 0.28 to 0.96), but shuffled labels give the same median (0.59).

The builder's two additions (matched odds under shuffled labels, the second permutation scheme) are correct. result.verdict:
The script is sound as a source of numbers. It runs clean from the repository root (134 s and 131 s, peak memory 1.19 GB), two runs gave byte-identical CSV files that also equal the committed copies, and every number I recomputed with independent code agrees: all of parts (a) to (f), all 612 cells of the linkage-group table, and every row of the position-control table from the same seed. Its checks are real; none is written so that it cannot fail. I found no wrong number, no data.table scoping error, no path or seed problem, and no breach of the memory or style rules.

The problem is what part (g) is read to show. The control it implements, as the task specified it, does not isolate position:
- **Whole run against random lists:** the run list holds whole genes (11,284 transcripts of 5,264 genes) and is compared with lists of single transcripts. Random sets of whole genes with the same isoform numbers and no position give a median of 1,072.5 terms with transcript totals (run 1,041) and 963 with line totals (run 555). The excess over 47 is the isoform unit of I-03 again.
- **Lists of the legacy size:** the excess of run lists with transcript totals (81 against 38) is mostly confinement to any 41% of the universe's genes (random whole-gene pools give a median of 62, other accession windows 66 to 92.5). Lists drawn from the five linkage groups alone give 43 to 44 against 38 to 40.
- **Line totals:** the run comes out low (36 against 43.5) because its transcripts have the most map lines each (2.14 against 1.79).

These comparison figures come from my scratch code, not from the script.

Two of the builder's corrections to issues.md are confirmed: the survivors are not from five linkage groups only, and "about doubles" holds only with one entry per transcript. Neither the current I-40 text nor the builder's proposed replacement should attribute the part (g) differences to position.

Recommended before issues.md is rewritten from this script: add a whole-gene comparison list to part (g) and reword its header, or keep the numbers and drop the word position. Accept. No reported number is wrong, and one medium finding should be fixed before the authors decide on I-05.

- **Runs:** two runs from the repository root exited with status 0 and no warning, in 348 s and 347 s with a peak of 1,602 MB on one core. The four CSV files are byte-identical between the two runs and to the copies I made beforehand. The script and its outputs in the repository are unchanged.

- **Checks:** four negative tests on a copy in a scratch root each stopped with the intended message: a DML row missing, a CpG missing from the corrected tables, a changed cutoff record, and one stored q-value changed by a relative 1e-6. The functions taken from the script by parsing agree with direct computation on synthetic inputs. The header's account of filterByCoverage and normalizeCoverage matches the installed methylKit 1.28.0 source, and its SLIM code uses no random numbers.
- **Rules of the task:** I found no typed-in result, no absolute path, no dependence on thread count or an unset seed, no data.table scoping hazard, no coordinate error and no non-ASCII character.

Findings:
- **Medium:** the script stops with a bare stopifnot when `import_min_coverage` is 1 or 10, the two other readings that I-05 offers.
- **Low:** the check on line 374 cannot fail, though nothing rests on it.
- **Low:** `libraries_with_changed_median` is 0 by construction for the rules that count libraries, and the table gives no margin.
- **Low:** two cutoffs are printed with floating-point noise.
